verification_performed.design_conformance: Exact match to lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md in all load-bearing details: infrastructure.ex's 17 children in verbatim order (ISS-0224 SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor-before-SandboxPool and ISS-0429 Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor-last both preserved, both re-stated as supervisor-boundary guarantees in the moduledoc, both test-backed in infrastructure_test.exs); pollers.ex's 2 gated children plus max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60 plus the pollers_init_probe seam; http.ex's single Bandit child under :start_http; application.ex's 3-child [Infrastructure, Pollers, Http] list under :one_for_one with the ISS-0429/decision-1 rationale restated inline; poller.ex's double-gated force_poller_crash guard as handle_info(:tick, state)'s first expression. Both compile_env gates (@supervisor_test_hooks_enabled? in pollers.ex, @poller_test_hooks_enabled? in poller.ex) reuse :activation_test_hooks_enabled? verbatim, exactly as designed -- confirmed by reading both attribute declarations and activation.ex's own precedent. This reuse is judged genuinely safe on independent OTP/idiom grounds, not merely deferred to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior acceptance: each module resolves its own compile-time literal independently from the same key, the key defaults false everywhere except config/test.exs, and each seam additionally requires an explicit runtime Application.put_env/3 call before it does anything -- so there is no cross-module leakage risk and no path by which enabling one seam silently activates another in any environment that matters. The only real cost is a naming smell (a third consumer makes the key's name under-describe what it now gates), which the design already flagged as an accepted, deferred cleanup, not a defect.
verification_performed.otp_idiom: All three new modules follow InstanceSupervisor's own use Supervisor / start_link/1 registering under __MODULE__ / init/1 returning Supervisor.init/2 convention. No GenServer wrapping a hand-rolled state machine anywhere in this diff -- this is a pure supervision-tree restructuring, gen_statem is not implicated. child_spec shapes are all copied byte-for-byte from the prior flat list (verified against the actual diff, not the design's paraphrase). :one_for_one over :rest_for_one at every level is justified against the real dependency graph: every named infra child (Repo, both Registries, all 7 Task.Supervisors, InstanceSupervisor) is looked up by name at its call sites in this codebase, never by stored pid -- consistent with existing precedent throughout lib/letflow/. Supervision isolation is preserved/improved, not collapsed: each instance-level concern (SandboxPool, PluginRegistry, etc.) still gets its own named, independently-restartable process; nothing here introduces a shared singleton or unsupervised spawn.

verification_performed.crash_cascade_finding_verdict: REAL, NOT PURELY A TEST ARTIFACT -- flagged for a follow-up issue, does not block this PASS. ELIXIR-DEV's framing ('fixed by clearing the crash-inducing env immediately after the first :DOWN', implying a test-only fix) undersells this. Reasoning: the crash-loop-to-budget-exhaustion cycle (zero-delay tick -> raise -> Pollers-level restart -> immediate re-tick -> raise again) is FAST enough that max_restarts: 5 is exhausted within a small fraction of the 60s window (confirmed by the test's own comments and independently by the 5-run-stable AC4 test timing). In the test, the only reason a SECOND full exhaustion-and-exit of Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers doesn't also happen (and potentially a third, within the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own default 3-restarts/5-seconds budget, taking the whole app down) is that the test process is an external actor that clears :force_poller_crash immediately after observing the first :DOWN. A real production fault that is PERSISTENT rather than self-clearing (e.g. a permanently misconfigured tenant schema, a permanently unreachable dependency the poller queries every tick) has no such external actor: the freshly-restarted Pollers would immediately re-enter the same crash-loop, exhaust its own 5/60 budget again on the same fast cadence, exit again, and repeat -- and because each full exhaustion-to-exit cycle is fast, multiple such Pollers-level exits could land within the top-level supervisor's own 5-second default window, exhausting ITS restart intensity too and taking down Letflow.Repo and Http with it. This is exactly the incident ISS-0425/REQ-219 exists to make structurally impossible, and REQ-219's chosen mechanism (isolate + bound restarts at the Pollers layer, single default-intensity restart at the top) fully closes it only for a TRANSIENT or self-clearing fault, not a persistent one. This does not fail REQ-219 as written -- decision 3's own text scopes AC4 to 'restarted ONCE by the top-level Supervisor' (a single occurrence), and ISS-0421's own text is already on record as deferring to REQ-219 for restart-intensity policy before deciding its own narrower fix -- but it is a genuine, non-hypothetical residual availability gap that should not be lost in test-comment text alone. RECOMMENDATION: ORCH should register a new issue (via letflow-queue, per ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- REVIEWER does not self-assign an ISS-NNNN id) titled along the lines of 'Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' crash-loop isolation only holds for a transient/self-clearing fault -- a persistent per-tick fault can still cascade to exhaust the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own restart intensity', tagged [otp, supervision, availability, s6], cross-referenced to ISS-0425/ISS-0421/REQ-219, and sequenced for whichever of ISS-0421's own follow-up or a new requirement is appropriate to decide the fix (e.g. a longer top-level intensity for this one child, exponential backoff before Pollers' own children re-tick after a layer restart, or a :significant/circuit-breaker mechanism).
